subject: Mobile deep-link blocked on corp device — Coupa onboarding flow
messages:
From: Olivia Torres <olivia.torres@supplylink.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mobile deep-link blocked on corp device — Coupa flow

Hi Marcus / Ben,

We tried to finish the Coupa vendor onboarding from an iPhone managed by our IT (company MDM). The activation link in the email opens the SupplyLink mobile deep-link (supplylink://onboard?token=...) but the flow drops the session after the first redirect and the app shows an error: "Activation failed: session missing". The same account works fine on desktop Chrome.

Attached: supplylink_screenshots.zip (screenshots of the error + the email deep link), onboard_redirect_logs.txt (server-side redirect traces).

Notes from the logs: the redirect chain includes a short-lived POST to /session/claim which returns 302 -> mobile-app-scheme. The mobile browser (Safari) seems to drop cookies on the handoff. IT says the device enforces a strict third-party cookie policy and blocks some cross-site cookie attributes.

Can you advise a fix or a safe manual activation path? We're in the final step for PO setup and ACME procurement is waiting on our supplier profile to go live.

Thanks,
Olivia Torres
Supplier Onboarding Lead
SupplyLink

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Torres <olivia.torres@supplylink.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mobile deep-link blocked on corp device — Coupa flow

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detail and the attachments, helpful.

Quick checklist while we dig in:
- Can you confirm the exact user-agent string and iOS version for the affected device?
- Please redact any SSNs/account numbers from the logs before sending new files.
- If possible, capture a HAR from Safari (or the in-app webview) and upload it to the Drive link we shared.

Ben — tagging you since this smells like a SameSite/hand-off edge case we saw with deep-links and Safari webviews last quarter. Laura, including you for security implications around cookie attributes and manual activation.

Interim ask for SupplyLink: any chance we can provide a one-click web activation (https://supplylink.com/activate?temp=...) that completes the claim entirely in the browser and avoids the mobile app scheme? If IT blocks third-party cookies, a browser-only activation may succeed.

I'll open an internal ticket and escalate if needed.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Partnerships Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Torres <olivia.torres@supplylink.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mobile deep-link blocked on corp device — Coupa flow

Short term workaround: if you can open the emailed activation link in Safari then use Private/Incognito mode (which isolates cookies) the handoff has worked in a few customer cases — the web session keeps the claim state when the app re-opens. Not ideal, but a quick test to validate whether it's the MDM cookie policy.

Longer term: we can add a query param fallback for deep-links: &web_fallback=1 that, when present, forces the server to render a small activation page (single POST) that completes the claim and returns a 200 rather than redirecting to the app scheme. That avoids cross-site cookie behavior during a POST->redirect. I'll file a follow-up engineering ticket if you want us to prioritize.

Attachment: sample_activation_payload.txt (example payload we can accept via the web endpoint).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Success — Supplier Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Torres <olivia.torres@supplylink.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mobile deep-link blocked on corp device — Coupa flow

Hi all,

Security note: Safari and many managed webviews enforce SameSite=Lax by default which can block cookies on POST-based redirects into custom schemes. If the activation sequence depends on an auth cookie set earlier in the chain, the browser may not send it during the redirect to supplylink:// which results in the "session missing" error.

Action items for SupplyLink (safe to share):
- Please send a redacted HAR (har_capture.har) showing request/response headers for the claim flow. We specifically need Set-Cookie attributes and the redirect responses.
- If you can, provide a temporary activation link that completes the claim inside the browser (no custom-scheme redirect). We can coordinate a short-lived manual activation token.

Operational constraints: we cannot put PII in public Drive links; use the secure upload link (see JIRA PROC-4421) or send logs over the secure portal. If logs contain personal data, redact before upload.

From a remediation perspective we recommend either:
1) Change the claim response to render an HTML success page (200) that instructs the app to poll for activation, or
2) Set cookie attributes to SameSite=None; Secure for the short-lived claim cookie and ensure the redirect is initiated from an HTTPS context.

I'll hold on the manual bypass until we confirm the log contents.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Torres <olivia.torres@supplylink.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mobile deep-link blocked on corp device — Coupa flow

Thanks — attaching the HAR (har_capture.har) and a trimmed redirect log (onboard_redirect_logs.txt). We redacted customer PII per your request.

Additional info from our IT: the MDM enforces an iOS configuration that disables cross-site cookies for browser-to-app handoffs unless the cookie is SameSite=None. Also they block universal links for third-party app schemes by default.

We can temporarily host a browser-only activation endpoint on staging. Can Redwood create a one-time activation token that we can call from that endpoint? If so we can complete the ACME onboarding today.

Attachments: har_capture.har, onboard_redirect_logs.txt

Olivia Torres
Supplier Onboarding Lead
SupplyLink
